shots.text: Brannoc broke the outer gate. Seraphel held the inner gate open with her back until the last of us were through. Then her light went out.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: Seraphel in the inner gate, armour drained of colour, sword blazing, holding the doors apart as the army runs past her. Her light goes out.

shots.text: Tell Ysolde I saw one more dawn. That was all I wanted.
shots.speaker: seraphel

shots.text: We found him in his ruined throne hall, on his knees. The monster's shape was cracking off him, and there was a tired man inside it.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: The throne hall in ruins. Vael-Orrun on his knees; the monster shape cracks, and a man in grey is inside it.

shots.text: I gave away my forgetting, so I remember everything. You should know what we did.
shots.speaker: thalassa
shots.art_note: The six Wardens standing round him. Thalassa steps forward.

shots.text: He kept the peace between us for forty years. We feared him, and we wanted his gold.
shots.speaker: thalassa
shots.art_note: A painted memory: the Feast of the Crossroads. A kind king in grey, his wife and small son, six crowned guests, all smiling.

shots.text:
They came to his feast as friends. At midnight they opened his gates. His city burned, and his wife and son burned with it.

The songs call it a victory. The Wardens call it the Night of Six Knives.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: The painting catches fire: the city of Vael burning at night, soldiers of six colours in the gates; the king on his knees in the ashes of the feast hall, holding a ring.

shots.speaker: ignar
shots.art_note: Ignar, his heart-light dim, head bowed.

shots.text: You did this. Remember that you did this.
shots.speaker: vael_orrun
shots.art_note: Vael-Orrun looking up at the six.

shots.speaker: thalassa
shots.art_note: Thalassa, bells silent in her hair, the only Warden who can meet his eyes.

shots.text:
That night a voice in the dark taught me how to make magic stop. I thought it was my own grief. It was never my own voice.

It is still listening.
shots.speaker: vael_orrun
shots.art_note: The grey going out of Vael-Orrun's eyes. He looks past the Wardens, at something behind the camera.

shots.text: Mirelle had seen a death at the end of the war. It was his.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: Mirelle at the edge of the hall, blind eyes glowing teal.

shots.text: Oswin pressed his lantern into the burning core in his chest. He turned to light, and the light went up out of the Hollow, home to Solenne, into the Heartstone that had been his crown.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: Oswin pressing the white lantern into the molten core behind Vael-Orrun's ribs. Vael-Orrun turns to white light, which rises through the stone sky.

shots.text:
He wanted the middle of the world. So we gave it to him. Not as its king.

As its light.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: Solenne at dawn: a beam of white light coming down out of the sky into the Hall of the Ring, and the Heartstone blazing.
